about: The gun deck of the frigate Commonwealth as built, 1797 (docs/shipkit-12): the planked deck under the guns, the spar deck's beams over it, its hatchways, wells and ladders, the gun deck's capstan, the pumps, the riding bitts, the galley, the bow's manger and cable scuttles, the captain's great cabin aft, the lanterns, and the guns' own gear. Lengths in feet (_ft) and inches (_in) unless a key says metres (_m). Each value carries its source; 'estimate' means period practice or proportion, not a drawing. gundeck.py reads this file

sources.gun_deck_1849: NARA 75841364, the gun deck plan in the Navy Yard Boston set of 1849 (with the spar deck plan, NARA 75841368, deck_1797.json), scale four feet to the inch (public domain; local copy in Data/Reference, measured only): the hatchways with their inside sizes written on them, the pumps either side of the main mast, the room between the after hatchways where the capstan stands, the riding bitts and the galley between the fore hatchway and the fore mast, the scuttle forward of it, the manger, the bulkhead and cabins aft
sources.spar_deck_1849: NARA 75841368 (deck_1797.json): the capstan's head, the companion, the skylights and the chimney over this deck; the gun deck's capstan, ladders, cabin and galley stand under them
sources.lines_1927: the 1927 lines (slices 1-2): the gun deck's sheer, the ports and the stern's windows
sources.period: estimate: the period's practice for an American or British frigate of the 1790s where neither drawing shows a part (the framing's sizes, the pumps, the stove, the cabin's joinery and furniture, the lanterns, the guns' implements and the lids' lanyards)

registration.note: the 1849 gun deck plan's full-resolution scan (3840 px wide), stern on the left, carried to the ship by the masts as the spar deck's plan is (deck_1797.json): between two masts an item keeps its share of the way from one to the other, aft of the mizzen and forward of the fore mast its distance from the mast at the plan's scale. The masts are where each one's axis passes the gun deck (spars.Rig's s_gun); the scale is the written sizes' (19.44 px a foot)

deck.note: the deck flat across (no round up, as the spar deck), its top on the skin's g_G row: the line under the port sills less 24 in (specs_1795.json inside.gun_deck_below_port_sill_in), faired between gun_deck_fair_m (specs_1795.json) where the traced sills left a kink (slice 8's known gap: the deck climbed 4 in in 5 m by port 10). Its underside 4 in below (the plank: the beams under it are the berth deck's, slice 13). The openings are open down to the wells (below); the masts, the capstan's barrel and the cable scuttles pass through holes. The pumps, bitts and stove stand on the deck, let into it

planking.note: pine plank 4 in thick and 7 in wide, laid as the spar deck's (deck_1797.json), the butts and plugs on its beams, which stand under the spar deck's (the same 32.7 in pitch from the waist's after end: estimate). Drawn by the material from the 'Planking' and 'Margin' UVs (build_frigate.py's GunDeckPlanks)

waterway.flush_note: the waterway timber's top lies flush with the planks for 12 in in from the side (the deck's 'Margin' UV: the material draws it as one oak timber, the planks nibbed into it where the deck narrows); only the cove above stands proud (estimate)
waterway.note: a small hollow (cove) along the deck's edge, 3 in out from the side and 2 in up it: the guns' carriages run out to within inches of the side, their trucks and the breeching bolts' rings over this corner, so the gun deck's waterway, a timber under the side's ceiling, shows only this much above the plank (estimate)

overhead.note: the spar deck's framing seen from the gun deck: its planks are 3 in thick (specs_1795.json inside.deck_slab_in: the placeholder's 8 in slab became the planks) on beams 14 in sided and 10 in moulded every other beam station (the waist's beams, deck_1797.json, carried on fore and aft), with a ledge between each two (6 by 5 in). Where a beam or ledge would cross an opening (a hatchway's coaming, the companion, a skylight, the chimney, a mast's partners, the capstan) it is cut: half beams from the side to a carling either side of the opening (8 by 8 in, fore and aft from the next whole beam to the next), and head ledges across between the carlings at the opening's ends. Under the gangways in the waist the stations between the waist's beams carry ledges out from the side to a carling under the opening's coaming; the waist's own beams (deck.py, across the open waist, their tops at the planks' underside) rest on the same clamp, their ends cut to the side, with their knees and stanchions as the beams here. A breast beam under each break, its face flush with the deck's edge. The beams' ends rest on a clamp along the side (10 in deep, 5 in thick; over each gun port its lower edge stands at least clamp_over_port_in over the port's head, clear of the housing bolts over the port (guns_1797.json: 58.5 in over the deck, the heads 53.6 to 55.6 in) and the housed gun's muzzle lashing through them), held by a hanging knee under each beam that comes between two ports (7 in sided, arms 30 in, its foot clear of the ports' linings; one that would come within an inch of a lid lanyard's cleat slides along under its beam to the beam's face); a stanchion (6 in, turned) under every second beam on the middle line where the room allows (all estimate, period practice for a frigate's upper deck)
overhead.chamfer_note: the beams', ledges' and carlings' lower edges chamfered (a beam's and a ledge's stopped short of the side, where the hanging and lodging knees and the clamp take its end, and of a carling; a carling's the whole way between the members its ends butt on): period joinery practice, sizes estimate

lodging_knee.note: a lodging knee at each end of each beam forward of the cabin (the whole and half beams and the waist's), lying flat in the angle between the beam's face and the side, its top flush with the beam's under the planks and sided_in deep: one arm along the beam's face (arm_beam_in), the other along the side (arm_side_in, or short_of_next_in short of the next member where that comes first, and none shorter than least_side_arm_in), each breadth_in broad at the throat and end_in at its end, the throat rounded to throat_in. On the face toward the ship's middle where that bay is clear_of_ports_m clear of the ports (the bays over them hold the implements and the lanyards), else on the other face; none where the side turns more than side_within_deg from fore and aft (the bow). Estimate: period practice for a frigate's upper deck, sizes from the hanging knees'

hatchways.note: the gun deck's openings (1849 gun deck plan, their inside sizes written on it; x from the plan through the masts, or under the spar deck's own where the two decks' hatches stand one over the other): each with a coaming, a grating over it (fair weather) or open as a ladderway. The wardroom's skylight (a grating over the light well to the wardroom below) is the plan's 4 ft 10 in long by 3 ft 1 in, narrowed to 2 ft 4 in so its coaming clears the second guns' train tackle bolts. The coaming 10 in high and 5 in thick (4 in round the skylight), the gratings as the spar deck's (estimate)

wells.note: under each opening a well down to the berth deck (slice 13 builds it): lined dark, its floor 7 ft 2 in below the gun deck's top, the berth deck's top (slice 13's line, handed to the orlop slice: the 1926 midship section's spacing, which sets her berth deck 17 ft 0 in over the rabbet amidships, where the 1795 section drawn from Humphreys' specifications has its lower deck). The ladders land on that floor

ladders.note: a ladder down each ladderway to the berth deck, from the hatch's after coaming forward (estimate), as the spar deck's (deck_1797.json); the companion's ladder from the quarterdeck's companion down to this deck, landing aft (estimate). The spar deck's four ladders at the breaks land on this deck in the waist: nothing stands within clear_m of their feet

capstan.note: the double capstan's lower head, on the gun deck under the spar deck's (deck_1797.json capstan, the same axis): its barrel (the spindle, 17 in) runs up through the gap between the decks to the spar capstan's barrel, and both heads turn together; worked by bars from both decks to heave the cables. Its own frame: origin on its axis at the gun deck's top, local Z up. Its pawls on the deck (period practice; sizes estimate)

bars.note: the capstan's bars, one for each hole (bar_holes), stowed overhead athwartships when the capstan is not manned: bars_a_bay side by side (gap_in apart) in the bays nearest the capstan clear of the ports, lanterns and openings, half each side, their outboard ends out_of_side_m in from the side, each set in two iron stirrups (stirrup_in: wide, thick) from the planks at stirrups_from_side_m, the bars' tops under the lodging knees. Each bar long_ft long, square (square_in) for square_long_in at its inner end to fit the drumhead's hole, then round, tapering from round_in[0] to round_in[1] at the hand. Estimate: period practice (capstan bars were stowed in racks overhead between the beams), sizes from the drumhead's holes

pumps.note: the 1849 plan's pumps either side of the main mast: aft of it the chain pumps (two chains in one case over the well, worked by a crank across the ship with a winch handle at each end; estimate: the period's chain pump), forward of it a pair of common (brake) pumps, their brakes pointing forward (estimate). Sizes estimate

bitts.note: the riding bitts abaft the fore mast (the 1849 plan's forward pair; its after pair stands where our galley's stove is): two posts through the deck with a cross piece on their fore faces and a standard (knee) behind each; bare at sea, the bowers' cables led below (estimate, sizes period practice)

galley.note: the galley under the forecastle, just abaft the riding bitts (where the 1849 plan has its after pair of bitts: bitts): an iron stove of the period's patent kind (Brodie's) on a brick hearth, its boilers' lids on top, the fire's open mouth and the oven's door on its fore face, a rail round it, its flue rising into the forecastle's chimney (deck_1797.json chimney) and meeting the chimney's plate. Sizes estimate

detail.note: how the stove is put together (estimate, from the period's cast-iron ship's stoves): cast plates bolted at angle irons (angle_in: leg, thickness) up the corners, round bolt heads bolt_in across at bolt_pitch_in; a band round the sides and after end at half height and a rib up each side's middle (band_in: width, proud); a fiddle bar round the top plate's edge (fiddle_in: high, square) to keep the pots on; an iron angle round the hearth's top edge (kerb_in: standing up, thick); the fire's open mouth with grate_bars bars grate_bar_in round across its lower part, the ash pit's door (ash_door_in) under it, and the oven's door on two strap hinges (hinge: strap width and thickness, knuckle, the strap's reach of the door's width) with a turned latch; a band and the damper's handle (damper_handle_in out) on the flue

bow.note: the bowers' cables come in through the hawse holes (anchors_1797.json, the bores now open to the gun deck), over the manger (a low board across the bow aft of the holes that stops the water coming in with the cables running aft) and down the cable scuttles to the tiers below (slice 14), lead collars round the scuttles. Sizes estimate
bow.scuttle_note: round, 20 in across for the 22 in (7 in thick) cable: room for it to turn down through the deck on its least bend (one and a half times its thickness) clear of the collar and the lining (estimate)

cabin.note: the captain's great cabin under the quarterdeck (1849 plan: the bulkhead and the state rooms; the 1797 cabin was the captain's on this deck, estimate): a panelled bulkhead across abaft the first guns with a door either side of the middle line (64 in high: the tiller's end and the tiller ropes sweep over their swing just above their heads, build.json gundeck.tiller_swing), the tiller ropes' runs aft through it in lead bushes near each side (tiller_ropes); inside, the dining cabin with the side lights, and aft the stern cabin under the windows with a state room in each quarter, a seat and lockers under the windows over the rudder's head. The deck covered with a painted floor cloth in black and white squares; a table and chairs, a sideboard and a lantern. All sizes estimate (period practice)

door_hang.note: each door hangs on two iron butt hinges at its outboard post, their pins' axis on the bulkhead's after face at the opening's edge (knuckle_in: diameter and length, 9 in in from the leaf's head and foot); the leaf is set recess_in in from that face, hinge_gap_in and latch_gap_in clear of its jambs (the latch side wide enough that the leaf's forward corner there clears the jamb as it swings), so it swings aft into the cabin clear of its jambs and casing up to open_deg. A low oak sill across the doorway sill_in over the deck; the leaf's foot under_in over the sill, or over the floor cloth where the deck rises aft under its swing if that is higher (all estimate, period joinery)

state_rooms.note: a state room in each quarter abaft fore_x_m and outboard of y_m: its inboard wall fore and aft, its door in it near the fore end (door_aft_of_fore_m), opening into the stern cabin (estimate)

seat.note: the window seat across the stern between the state rooms (estimate, period cabin joinery): deep_in deep and high_in high, the rudder's head boxed inside it (rudder_box_in clear); a hinge rail hinge_rail_in deep let into the after wall, lids_a_side lids each side before it on brass hinges (hinge_in: knuckle long and round; the piece over the rudder's head is fixed, middle_beyond_box_in past its box), gap_in between the pieces, the top top_in thick with its nosing (nosing_in over the front) rounded over; the front board framed (stile_in stiles, bottom_rail_in and top_rail_in rails) with raised and fielded panels no wider than panel_max_in (frame_proud_in: the frame's and the fields' faces off the board; field_inset_in the bevel's width)

cabin.chairs_note: each chair [x m, y m, the way its sitter faces (deg, 0 forward, 90 to starboard)]: one at each end of the table (72 in long fore and aft, 40 in across) and two a side

sideboard.note: against the bulkhead's after face on the starboard side, 20 in deep, 54 in long, 36 in high

after_wall.note: the after wall (the stern's inside, raked as the gun rows end) with the three stern windows opened through it and the transom: each window's inside opening reveal_in larger all round than the glass, the reveal lined between them with lining_in board (an inch board planed, mitred at the corners), its face lining_in inside the glass's edge where it butts on the glass, behind the sash's frame

panelling.note: the after wall's joinery between the state rooms, laid on its rake (estimate, period cabin joinery: a captain's cabin was panelled and painted): a sill rail along the seat's top under the windows (sill_out_in out), a pilaster between each two windows (pilaster_in: wide, out) on a base (base_in: high, out past the pilaster) under a capital (capital_in: high, out past it) and a stile at each end (stile_in wide), a head moulding over each window (head_in: high, out) and a raised and fielded panel over that (field_out_in, field_inset_in), and a cornice under the spar deck's planks (cornice_in high, its fascia fascia_out_in out and its ovolo cornice_out_in out); every piece clear_in clear of a window's opening

cabin.lights_note: the cabin's side light each side (slice 9's sash and glass, decor_1797.json cabin_window) is a port in the port band with no lid, cut through the side as the gun ports are (specs_1795.json cabin_lights_m): daylight comes in through it

tiller.note: the tiller overhead in the great cabin (Bean's choice, Nov 18 2026: the British frigates' way; Constitution's own tiller worked on the berth deck below, museum_1812). The rudder's head is the blade's main piece squared on up from the blade's top along the line the rudder turns about (skin.py rudder_axis: 1 px abaft the sternpost's aft face, which stands 7 degrees abaft upright there): head_in fore and aft (from the blade's fore face) and athwartships, its corners rounded head_corner_in, head_into_blade_in down into the blade's top. It comes up through the window seat's fixed middle (cut round all it sweeps, seat_hole_clear_in clear; the seat's front stands seat_front_clear_in before its sweep) in front of the middle stern window, to head_clear_in clear of the quarterdeck's beams at every angle of the helm, its top cut parallel to the tiller. An iron hoop round it either side of the mortise (hoop_in broad and thick, hoop_gap_in off the mortise, top_over_hoop_in under the top). The iron tiller (museum_1812: an iron tiller; forged square, tapering from root_in at the head to end_in, wide by deep) goes through the mortise and is keyed abaft the head (tang_aft_in, key_in thick, broad and long), and runs forward under the beams, gap_under_beams_in clear of each all along at every angle (the way to the nearest of them, not only straight up), length_m from the head's axis to the middle of its end eye (end_eye_in: a ring across and its bar round, the arm necking down into it over neck_in: long, wide and deep at the ring), the tiller ropes spliced round the ring (tiller_ropes). The head, its hoops and the tiller are one object (Tiller) that swings about the head's axis, hard_over_deg either way, clear of all round it (the build turns it step by step and fails on a touch or less than half an inch); a positive turn about its frame's Z takes the tiller to starboard and the ship's head to port, as the wheel's positive turn does. The blade stays as built (its lower pintles stand off that axis, where the sternpost bends). All sizes estimate (period practice; a 44's tiller about 15 to 18 ft)

tiller_ropes.note: the tiller rope (deck_1797.json wheel: tiller_rope_in round, wound rope_turns on the barrel) from the wheel's two legs to the tiller's end eye: each leg (the starboard leg abaft the port one, deck_1797.json wheel legs_x_m) comes down through the quarterdeck's planks between the cheeks of its leading sheave's chock, bolted up under the deck in the bay before the cabin's bulkhead, which turns it out athwartships under the beams; run_off_middle_m out from the middle line a side sheave turns it aft, along under the beams and through a lead bush in the cabin's bulkhead (bush_in: bore, rim across, rim proud, the lining's wall), to an after sheave abaft the tiller's end at after_x_m that turns it in to the end eye, where it is spliced round the ring's bar (eye_in: the eye's inside length past the bar, the splice's length). Hauling in the starboard rope takes the tiller to starboard (deck.py wheel: a turn of the wheel's top to port hauls it in). Every sheave (sheave_in: across its rim and thick, the rope's middle rope_in_groove_in in from the rim, in a groove 0.05 in clear of it) turns on an iron pin (pin_in: round, its head across and thick) between two oak cheeks (cheek_in: thick, their rim out past the sheave's) slot_clear_in clear of it each side, an oak crown between them crown_clear_in clear of the rope (crown_in thick); the level sheaves hang under the planks on an oak stool (stool_in square, let_in into the planks), the leading ones' cheeks run up into the planks. Every run lies level with the end eye's ring at rest, under the beams. The after sheaves stand abaft the tiller's end, where the two ropes from them to the eye never ask for more rope than amidships at any angle of the helm (the build fails if they do): the easing rope takes up the difference as slack (build.json gundeck.tiller_ropes.slack_in, by angle). As the helm goes over each rope's eye slides round the ring to face its sheave and its run (from the sheave to the splice) swings and shortens or lengthens: TillerEye_S and TillerEye_P turn on their frames, TillerRun_S and TillerRun_P are posed and stretched along their own X, every degree (gundeck.json tiller_ropes.poses); the build turns them all with the tiller, step by step, and fails on a touch or less than half an inch. All sizes estimate (period practice: blocks for a 3 in rope about 10 to 12 in long)

lanterns.note: horn lanterns: one between each second pair of guns a side (between_guns), hung between the spar deck's beams on a hook in the planks' underside, in the bay nearest the middle between the two ports that stands clear of both (clear_of_ports_m: the bays over the ports hold the guns' implements) and in_from_side_m in from the side's inner face, over the room between the two guns and out of the walk fore and aft inboard of them (fighting lanterns hung at the side between the guns: estimate); and one over the cabin's table, up in the skylight over it (the tiller swings under the beams below), on a bar across under the skylight's ridge, its ends let into the gable ends (cabin_bar_in sided and moulded, its top cabin_bar_under_ridge_in under the ridge). Each a light in the game data (gundeck.json lights): warm candle light. Sizes estimate

light.lumens_note: set for the game's exposure below decks, not a candle's: a tallow candle gives about 12 lm and a horn lantern passes less than that, so a period gun deck at night was far darker than the game shows it (the PC lighting lane tunes it against the exposure, VisualPipeline's incident meter)

cabin_light.note: the cabin's lantern hangs 2.2 m abaft the bulkhead, up in the skylight: it casts shadows so its light stops at the bulkhead (unshadowed it lit the deck 5 m forward of it), out of its own lantern's mesh (which casts none)

lanterns.zones_note: each light is in a zone (gun_deck, great_cabin): in the game a light should light only the objects of its own zone (lighting channels: gundeck.json below.zones), or, unshadowed, it shines through the planks onto the spar deck's guns and the berth deck below, and through the side onto the sea and the channels. The deck's lanterns reach no further than the cabin's bulkhead (each one's radius_m stops short of its fore face) and the cabin's casts shadows, so neither shines through the bulkhead

light_budget.note: fourteen lanterns, unshadowed, and the cabin's, shadowed (its radius 4 m); the ports and hatches give daylight: no light probes below in this slice (the PC lane's to add if the frame allows)

gun_gear.note: each long gun's gear (slice 8 left it for here). Housed for sea, a wooden tompion in the muzzle and a lead apron over the vent and the lock (taken out and off when the guns are cast loose, so only in Guns_Housed). Over each gun, athwartships in the bay between the spar deck's beams over its port, its two staffs (the sponge and rammer on one, the ladle and worm on the other, as sea service carried them) and its two handspikes, each on two iron hangers with a hook, hung below the beams so they pass under the carlings; its shot in a garland on the deck against the waterway in the space forward of its port; each lid's two lanyards (the hinges' straps end in a ringbolt on the lid's outside) up the side to lead-lined holes over the port, in through them and down to a cleat beside it (outside, lying down the shut lid with the guns housed, taut to the open lid with them run in or out). Sizes estimate (period practice)

implements.note: each staff ash, 2 in, 10 ft between its heads: the sponge (a fleece-covered head a hair over the bore, 5.9 in, 12 in long) and the rammer (5.6 in, 7 in) on one, the worm (two iron prongs in a 5 in double spiral, 6 in) and the ladle (a copper scoop 5.4 in across, 22 in long, holding the 8 lb charge, open a third of its round) on the other, each head on an iron ferrule; the handspikes ash, 6 ft, 3 by 2.5 in at the butt, its toe bevelled over handspike_toe_in[0] to handspike_toe_in[1] thick, tapering to a round grip. They lie side by side across the bay (the heads' widths and gap_in apart), the outboard ends in_from_side_in off the side, their tops below_beam_in under the beams' underside; each on two hangers (0.5 in iron rods from screw eyes in the deck's underside) ending in a 3 in hook, either side of its middle (in the waist: waist)

waist.note: In the waist only the gangways are over the guns, so a staff laid athwartships over the gun would reach out under open sky with nothing to hang its inboard end from. There each gun's set hangs fore and aft under its gangway instead, its middle over the port's, the innermost item edge_in outboard of the gangway's inner edge, each item on two hangers at hangers_at of its length.

garland.note: a rail of oak 5 in wide and 3.5 in high lying on the deck along the waterway's cove, its length cupped for eight 24 lb shot (5.55 in) pitch_in apart, cup_in deep; one for each gun in the space forward of its port (the foremost in the space before the bridle port), clear of the ports by port_clear_in at least

lanyard.note: two to a lid, over its hinges' straps: an eyebolt through the lid at the strap's end (ring_from_hinge_of_lid of the lid's height down from the hinge) with a ring in it; the lanyard (1.5 in rope) spliced to the ring, up to a hole 2.25 in across bored through the side and the clamp over the port (hole_over_clamp_edge_in over the clamp's lower edge there, which stands clear of the housing bolts, or lower where the clamp is eased so shallow over a port that the bush's rim would come within a quarter inch of its top; past the clamp's ends hole_above_head_in over the port's head, inside or out, whichever is the higher) and lined with lead (a bush each face, bush_in across and proud; a chain plate over the port stops an inch above the outer bush: standing_1797.json chain_note), in through it and down the inside to a cleat beside the port (cleat_out_of_jamb_in along the side's face from the jamb as it is on the inner face, cleat_over_deck_in up; the cleat and both bushes lie on the faces square to them and stand on the planking as built), belayed there with its tail hanging plumb; its runs down the inside (bush to cleat, and the tail) lie taut over the side's inner face, the clamp and the waterway, lay_off_in off them. Outside it lies down the shut lid over the hinge, and runs taut to the open lid's ring. The bushes and cleats are LanyardFittings, the rope inside (and outside the bridle ports' lids, which never open) LidLanyards

port_stops.note: a stop round the inside of each gun port with a lid, for the lid to close against: the lid is the planking's cut-out less a quarter inch all round and as thick as the planking, so it bears on the frames' outer face, and the port's opening through the frames is narrower than the cut-out by the stop's lap (the period's rabbet round a port, estimate). Each stop stands proud_in into the opening from the lining (lapping the shut lid by half an inch), deep_in along the side's normal, its outer face off_lid_in inboard of the lid's inner face, its back let let_in into the lining; the sill's and head's run from jamb to jamb and the jambs' between them. With the lid shut no daylight shows round it (build.json gundeck.lid_light); with it open the stops are the shoulder the lid sat on

budget_note: the plan's figure for slice 12 (the gun deck, loaded only when below: build.json gundeck.triangles_below): a starting point, not a ceiling (Bean, Nov 12: frame rate is the only hard limit), so the build reports the count against it and never fails on it

meets.note: the gun deck's parts that meet another part of the ship (or each other) by design, each pair with why and how far (in) either may go into the other; every other meeting fails the build (build_frigate's gundeck_room, deck.room). Each entry: the parts on one side, the parts on the other, why, the depth allowed (measured, plus a quarter inch, rounded up to a twentieth). A designed contact the build no longer finds fails it too: a part meant to stand on, be let into or rest against another that no longer reaches it hangs clear of what holds it
pairs: the after wall's edges against the side's inner face
the after wall's top under the spar deck's planks
the state rooms' inboard walls run aft to the after wall, their ends let into its rake
each window's lining fills the after wall's opening for it
the window seat's top is let into the after wall
the cabin's bulkhead is scribed round the clamp at the side
the cabin's bulkhead stands on the deck, its foot let in where the sheer rises under it
the cabin's bulkhead's ends are scribed to the side's inner face
the cabin's bulkhead's ends are scribed down over the waterways
the cabin's bulkhead's head under the spar deck's planks
the cabin's table, chairs and lockers stand on the floor cloth
each stirrup's straps go up into the planks over the capstan bars, bolted through them
the spar deck's beams' ends rest on the clamp, let down into it
the clamp is bolted to the side's inner face, which curves under its back
each hanging knee's arm is fayed over the clamp
the lid lanyards' holes are bored through the clamp over each port, lined with their lead bushes
the state rooms' fore walls are scribed round the clamp at the side
the waist's beams' ends rest on the clamp as the deck beams' do
the rammers, sponges, worms and ladles hang on hooks driven into the beams
each hanging knee's upper arm is fayed to its beam's side
each lodging knee's arm is fayed to its beam's face
the spar deck's planks are laid on its beams
each stanchion's head is under its beam
